learn.title: The Duck Curve Problem
learn.intro: Solar energy's rapid growth creates a unique challenge: a sharp drop in grid supply at sunset, requiring quick backup power. This 'duck curve' demonstrates the need for flexible energy systems to balance renewables with grid stability.
learn.c1_text: Solar panels generate 70% of daily energy in California, but production plummets 90% in 1 hour at sunset. This sudden drop forces utilities to ramp up gas plants rapidly to avoid blackouts.
learn.c2_text: Traditional grids rely on steady baseload power, but solar's variability requires 30% faster response times from backup generation. Battery storage and demand-response programs help smooth this transition.
learn.c3_text: India plans 15 GW of grid-scale battery storage by 2025 to address solar curtailment issues. Gujarat's 100 MW / 4-hour storage project in Ahmedabad demonstrates this solution in action.
learn.stat1: India: 11 GW solar curtailed in 2023-24 due to grid constraints
learn.stat2: California's duck curve reduced gas use by 25% through demand-response programs
learn.stat3: Germany's 10 GW battery storage capacity avoids 20% of solar curtailment losses
learn.stat4: Global grid flexibility investments needed: $1.3 trillion by 2030

learn.title: Virtual Power Plants
learn.intro: Virtual power plants (VPPs) use AI to coordinate millions of decentralized energy assets, transforming them into a single responsive grid resource. This innovation is crucial for integrating distributed renewables.
learn.c1_text: Singapore's 1 GW VPP connects 60,000 solar rooftops and 20,000 EV batteries, providing 100 MW of grid support during peak demand. AI predicts and manages 200+ energy sources in real-time.
learn.c2_text: VPPs can respond 100 times faster than conventional plants to grid fluctuations. In Australia, a 50 MW VPP reduced AEMO's frequency deviations by 40% during 2023's solar peak.
learn.c3_text: India's 100 GW rooftop solar potential could power 5 VPPs equivalent to 10 GW each. Tamil Nadu's 50 MW VPP project in Chennai demonstrates this scalable approach.
learn.stat1: India: 10,000+ MW rooftop solar potential for VPP integration
learn.stat2: Singapore's VPP reduced grid costs by $120 million annually
learn.stat3: Australia's VPPs provide 15% of grid stability services
learn.stat4: Global VPP market to reach $100 billion by 2030

learn.title: Electric Commercial Vehicles
learn.intro: Transitioning buses and trucks to electric power reduces urban pollution and creates grid integration opportunities. Heavy vehicles account for 40% of transport emissions globally.
learn.c1_text: Modern electric trucks use 800V systems to charge in 15 minutes, vs 90 minutes for 400V systems. A 750 kWh battery powers 500 km for heavy-duty EVs, equivalent to 100% of India's 2023 truck emissions reduction target.
learn.c2_text: Battery-to-grid (V2G) technology lets trucks return 30% of stored energy to the grid during shortages. In California, 10 electric trucks provide 1 MW of responsive power capacity.
learn.c3_text: India aims for 500,000 electric trucks by 2030 under FAME II. Tata's 32-tonne electric truck in Mumbai demonstrates 18% lower TCO vs diesel alternatives.
learn.stat2: China's electric trucks save $0.10/km vs diesel
learn.stat3: Global EV truck sales to reach 10 million units by 2030

learn.title: HVDC Transmission
learn.intro: High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) lines transmit power 3x more efficiently than AC over long distances, enabling continental-scale renewable energy sharing.
learn.c1_text: HVDC reduces transmission losses to 3% vs 7% for AC over 1,000 km. China's 2,900 km Zhangjiakou-Beijing line transmits 12 GW with 50% less land use.
learn.c2_text: HVDC cables like Germany's 1,450 km Nord Stream 2 transmit 55% more power than equivalent AC lines. This enables offshore wind integration across regions.
learn.c3_text: India's 5 GW offshore wind target requires 3 HVDC corridors by 2030. The 450 km Kanyakumari-Mumbai line will transmit 3 GW with 99.9% reliability.
learn.stat3: Global HVDC market to reach $18 billion by 2030

learn.title: Climate Finance & COP Agreements
learn.intro: International climate finance mechanisms like the Green Climate Fund ($100B+ pledged) determine how developing countries access renewable energy transitions.
learn.c1_text: The $275 billion Global Energy Alliance for People & Planet (GEAPP) launched at COP28 aims to triple global renewables by 2030 through cross-border investments.
learn.c2_text: COP26's $100B/year climate finance pledge remains $20B short. India's $1.4 trillion renewable target requires $1.2 trillion in international funding by 2030.
learn.c3_text: India received $3.2 billion from the Green Climate Fund (2021-2025) for solar projects. The PM-KUSUM scheme leverages $500 million in international co-financing.

learn.stat4: COP28 renewable energy pledge: $1 trillion by 2030

learn.title: Offshore Wind Farms
learn.intro: Offshore wind harnesses stronger coastal winds to generate 3x more power per turbine than onshore, with India targeting 30 GW by 2030.
learn.c1_text: Floating wind turbines at 100+ meters depth use 200-ton steel platforms. Norway's Hywind Tampen farm generates 250 MW for 44,000 homes, equivalent to 100% of Svalbard's energy needs.
learn.c2_text: Submarine cables transmit 1 GW+ power to shore with 99.9% efficiency. Vietnam's 300 MW offshore project uses dynamic positioning systems to maintain alignment in typhoon zones.
learn.c3_text: India's first 2.5 GW offshore wind zone in Gujarat will use 150+ turbines. The 30 GW target requires 12 GW of HVDC corridors by 2030.
